results.title: Swedish startup Strawberry launches AI browser for non-technical teams
results.content:
Most AI assistants live in a chat window. Stockholm-based Strawberry wants them to work where people already do their jobs: inside the browser, with access to the tabs, tools, and accounts they use every day.

The startup released version 1.0 of its AI browser today, taking it out of beta and pitching it at workers who do not write code.

That includes people in sales, marketing, recruitment and customer service, who often rely on the same repetitive browser-based tasks but lack the time or technical skills to automate them.

Strawberry calls its AI assistants “companions”. Users train them to handle specific jobs, and the assistants learn how a team works over time, the company said. [...] The company wants to make that expertise available to an entire team rather than leave it with the person who knows how to get the most out of an AI tool.

Version 1.0 also adds a way to capture video meetings on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet directly from a user’s computer. Because the recording happens locally, no separate bot needs to join the call. Strawberry then turns the conversation into notes and follow-up tasks.

The pitch puts Strawberry somewhere between general-purpose AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude, and personal assistants such as Meta’s Muse.

Rather than asking employees to switch to another chat app, Strawberry wants its companions to work across the browser-based services they already use. [...] The biggest change in version 1.0 is that this knowledge can now be shared. A salesperson, for example, could train a companion to research potential clients, contact them, and enter their details into a sales database.

Once trained, the companion can be used by colleagues across the team, without each person having to start from scratch.

Companions can also work on a schedule or start when a new email or sales lead arrives. For larger jobs, such as researching 200 companies, one companion can divide the work among several sub-agents running in parallel.

> “Today the person who is great with Claude keeps all of it on their own laptop,” said Charles Maddock, Strawberry’s chief executive and co-founder.

results.title: Strawberry Is The Best AI Browser I Have Used - Make Tech Easier
results.content:
At the core of Strawberry are AI agents called Companions. These agents can click through websites, fill out forms, extract data, and manage multiple tabs to complete workflows that would normally take hours. The browser ships with several specialized Companions for different use cases, such as Sales Sally for sales teams and Recruiter Ryan for recruiters. There are also Companions designed for marketing, business, and other professional functions. [...] [mte\_toc]

## What is Strawberry?

Strawberry is a new kind of web browser built around the idea of autonomous AI agents that can take action on your behalf. Instead of being a static tool for viewing websites, it acts as an intelligent workspace that understands instructions and completes tasks automatically. The company behind it calls it an “agentic browser,” meaning it can go beyond simply displaying pages and actually perform actions within them. [...] Another major difference is that Strawberry has been built from the ground up as a standalone browser designed for automation. It is not an extension or plugin that sits on top of Chrome. This gives it deeper control and better integration across multiple tabs and sites. The browser is also geared more toward professional use than casual browsing. Its design focuses on automating workflows common in sales, recruitment, research, and operations, areas where repetitive web tasks can easily take up large portions of the day.
